statements.status_notes: Waiting for upstream fixes in Debian trixie.
Waiting for upstream fixes in Debian trixie.

CVE-2026-53615 is a libblkid DOS-partition bounds/overflow issue, reachable only when libblkid parses a block device or disk image. datahub-actions never parses block devices (Python event processor; no blkid/fdisk/partition tooling in its runtime), so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2026-53614 is a libmount SUID-hardening issue affecting restricted users invoking a multi-step legacy mount(2). datahub-actions runs nonroot and never invokes mount, so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2026-53613 is a libmount TOCTOU on the mount target, reachable only while mounting a filesystem. datahub-actions never performs mount operations (Python event processor, nonroot), so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2026-53612 is a libmount fd-based ownership/mode flaw exercised during a mount operation. util-linux ships here only as a base-OS package; datahub-actions is a Python event-processing app that runs nonroot and never performs mount operations (no mount/umount, no libmount-using tooling in its runtime), so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2025-70873 is an information disclosure in zipfileInflate, part of the zipfile virtual-table extension that Debian compiles into the sqlite3 CLI package. This image installs only libsqlite3-0 3.46.1-7+deb13u1 (a transitive library dependency of the bundled CPython); the sqlite3 CLI is not installed, so the zipfile extension code is not present. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13-dev image: `command -v sqlite3` finds no binary and dpkg lists only libsqlite3-0 from the sqlite3 source package.

CVE-2026-53615 is a libblkid DOS-partition bounds/overflow issue, reachable only when libblkid parses a block device or disk image. datahub-actions never parses block devices (Python event processor; no blkid/fdisk/partition tooling in its runtime), so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2024-21503 is a ReDoS in black's lines.py (fixed in black 24.3.0), triggerable only when black formats crafted source code. As with CVE-2026-32274 in this file, black 22.3.0 is an SBOM false positive: acryl-datahub declares it in a dev-only extra, but the package is NOT installed in any variant. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 and 1.5.0.7-debian13-full images: no black distribution exists under /opt/datahub/lib/python3.10/site-packages and no /opt/datahub/bin/black entry point exists. The vulnerable formatter cannot execute because black itself is not present.

CVE-2026-53614 is a libmount SUID-hardening issue affecting restricted users invoking a multi-step legacy mount(2). datahub-actions runs nonroot and never invokes mount, so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

SBOM false-positive: black 22.3.0 is listed in /opt/docker/sbom/datahub-actions/.spdx.datahub-actions.json because acryl-datahub declares it in a dev-only extra, but the package is NOT installed in any variant. Verified: `pip show black` returns 'Package(s) not found' on the dhi/datahub-actions:1-dev image; `find /opt -name 'black*'` returns only /opt/datahub/lib/python3.10/site-packages/datahub/ingestion/sink/blackhole.py (datahub's no-op metadata sink, unrelated to the black formatter). The vulnerable code path (black formatting a maliciously-named source file with path traversal) cannot execute because black itself is not present.

CVE-2026-53613 is a libmount TOCTOU on the mount target, reachable only while mounting a filesystem. datahub-actions never performs mount operations (Python event processor, nonroot), so the vulnerable code path is not executed. No fix is available in Debian trixie.

CVE-2025-15649 is in the IO::Uncompress::Unzip perl module, which ships in perl-modules-5.40. The datahub-actions -dev variants install only stock debian perl-base 5.40.1-6; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13-dev image: no Unzip.pm exists on the filesystem and `perl -MIO::Uncompress::Unzip -e 1` fails with "Can't locate IO/Uncompress/Unzip.pm in @INC", so the vulnerable code is not present.

No fix is available in Debian trixie.

The datahub-actions -dev variants install only stock debian perl-base 5.40.1-6; perl-modules-5.40 is not installed. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13-dev image: `command -v zipdetails` finds no binary and no IO/Compress tree exists under any @INC path (`perl -MIO::Compress::Gzip -e 1` cannot locate the module), so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-7010 is a CRLF injection in the HTTP::Tiny perl module (fixed upstream in HTTP::Tiny 0.093, unfixed in trixie). The scanner attributes it to the shared perl source package, but HTTP::Tiny ships in perl-modules-5.40, which the datahub-actions -dev variants do not install: they carry only stock debian perl-base 5.40.1-6 (via .apt.debian-13.inc.yaml). Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13-dev image: no HTTP/Tiny.pm exists anywhere on the filesystem and `perl -MHTTP::Tiny -e 1` fails with "Can't locate HTTP/Tiny.pm in @INC", so the vulnerable code is not present.

CVE-2026-48962 is a CWE-95 eval sink in File::GlobMapper (part of IO::Compress, perl-modules-5.40) reachable via an attacker-controlled output glob. The datahub-actions -dev variants install only stock debian perl-base (5.40.1-6); perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and File::GlobMapper / IO::Compress are absent from disk (`perl -MIO::Compress::Gzip -e1` fails to locate it on the built 1-dev image). The vulnerable code is not shipped; the scanner flags it via perl-base sharing the `perl` source package. Per-image statement needed because the org-wide vex/debian/dhi-perl.vex.json covers 48962 only for the DHI-rebuilt perl@5.40.1-6+dhiN, not the stock perl these dev variants ship.

CVE-2024-26461 is a memory leak in lib/gssapi/krb5/k5sealv3.c, the GSSAPI per-message seal/unseal path in libgssapi-krb5-2, with no fix planned by Debian. The leaking code runs only inside an established GSS-API security context. In this image GSSAPI is reachable only through libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit when an operator explicitly configures SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) for the Kafka event source or an ingestion source against their own KDC and brokers; the image binds no GSSAPI-authenticated listener (the framework is a Kafka client and GMS REST client, verified package set and entrypoint on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image). An unauthenticated adversary has no channel to feed GSS tokens to this code; per-message tokens arrive only from operator-trusted brokers inside an operator-established security context, so the leak cannot be driven by an adversary.

CVE-2026-48962 is a CWE-95 eval sink in File::GlobMapper (part of IO::Compress, perl-modules-5.40) reachable via an attacker-controlled output glob. The datahub-actions -dev variants install only stock debian perl-base (5.40.1-6); perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and File::GlobMapper / IO::Compress are absent from disk (`perl -MIO::Compress::Gzip -e1` fails to locate it on the built 1-dev image). The vulnerable code is not shipped; the scanner flags it via perl-base sharing the `perl` source package. Per-image statement needed because the org-wide vex/debian/dhi-perl.vex.json covers 48962 only for the DHI-rebuilt perl@5.40.1-6+dhiN, not the stock perl these dev variants ship.

CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c, the ONC RPC portmapper helper in libgssrpc, with no fix planned by Debian. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: libgssrpc.so.4 is present only as a dependency of the krb5-user kadmin/kpasswd client tools; no long-running process links it. The entrypoint chain (start.sh -> python datahub-actions, plus the JRE only inside the executor's ingest subprocess on full variants) never loads libgssrpc and the image binds no RPC listener, so the leaking path runs only when an operator interactively invokes kadmin.mit against an admin server they chose. An adversary has no channel to drive the leak, and a memory leak in a short-lived operator-invoked CLI yields no denial-of-service leverage.

CVE-2018-5709 is an integer truncation of dbentry->n_key_data in kadmin/dbutil/dump.c, code that compiles into the kdb5_util KDC database tool shipped by Debian's krb5-kdc/krb5-admin-server packages. This image installs only krb5-config, krb5-user and the MIT runtime libraries. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: kdb5_util, kadmind and krb5kdc exist in neither /usr/bin nor /usr/sbin (only the krb5-user client tools such as kinit.mit, klist.mit and kadmin.mit ship), so the vulnerable database-dump code is not present.

The datahub-actions -dev variants install only stock debian perl-base (5.40.1-6, via .apt.debian-13.inc.yaml + build-essential); perl-modules-5.40 is not installed and the module is absent from disk (`perl -MIO::Uncompress::Unzip -e1` fails to locate it on the built 1-dev image). The scanner attributes the CVE to the shared `perl` source package via the installed perl-base, but the vulnerable code is not shipped. Per-image statement needed because the org-wide vex/debian/dhi-perl.vex.json covers 48959 only for the DHI-rebuilt perl@5.40.1-6+dhiN, not the stock perl these dev variants ship; CVE-2026-42496/42497/9538 on the same stock perl@5.40.1-6 are already covered org-wide by vex/debian/perl.vex.json.

CVE-2025-14017 is a flaw in libcurl's LDAPS (LDAP-over-TLS) handling: in multi-threaded transfers a TLS-option change in one thread can disable certificate verification for concurrent LDAPS transfers. curl carries LDAP support here (libldap2 is installed), but datahub-actions invokes curl only for HTTP health polling (start.sh curls the GMS /health gate); it never performs LDAPS transfers, let alone concurrent multi-threaded ones, so the vulnerable code path is not executed.

CVE-2025-15224 (curl advisory 'libssh key passphrase bypass without agent set') is specific to curl's libssh backend, which could wrongly fall back to authenticating via a locally running ssh-agent during SCP/SFTP public key authentication. Debian builds curl 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 against libssh2; the libssh backend is compiled out. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1, so the vulnerable libssh code path is not present.

CVE-2025-15079 (curl advisory 'libssh global known_hosts override') is specific to curl's libssh backend: with CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS set, the libssh backend could still accept SCP/SFTP hosts recognized only via libssh's global known_hosts file. Debian builds curl 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 against libssh2; the libssh vssh backend is compiled out. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1, so the vulnerable libssh code path is not present.

The leaking code runs only inside an established GSS-API security context. CVE-2025-10966 is missing SSH host verification in curl's wolfSSH-powered SFTP backend. Debian builds curl/libcurl4t64 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 against libssh2, not wolfSSH; curl supports exactly one SSH backend per build, so the wolfSSH code is compiled out. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: `curl --version` reports libssh2/1.11.1 and no wolfSSH, so the vulnerable backend code is not present.

GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf is an out-of-bounds read in the OpenSSL that the cryptography project statically bundles into its prebuilt PyPI wheels (fixed only in the 48.0.1 wheel; the advisory notes sdist installs are unaffected because they link the system OpenSSL). This image installs cryptography from sdist (uv --no-binary cryptography), so it builds against and dynamically links the patched system OpenSSL; the vulnerable bundled OpenSSL is not present in the image.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

False positive. CVE-2026-22184 affects the untgz utility that is part of zlib source code, but Debian zlib packages (zlib1g and zlib1g-dev) do not ship the untgz utility by default. For Debian Trixie (and other versions), zlib comes from zlib1g (binaries) and does not include the untgz binary. The vulnerability scanner incorrectly flags zlib packages as vulnerable when the untgz utility is not actually present in the installed packages.
